sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology and Industrials cement their market leadership as all-green sectors, while Financials show early signs of positive rotation despite a low YTD standing.

On 2026-06-22, US sector breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 3 of 11 groups achieving "all-green" status (positive across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons). Technology continues to dominate the leaderboard, holding the rank 1 spot with a momentum score of 0.99. Industrials (momentum 0.79) joins Tech as a sustained leader over the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons, signaling robust demand for cyclical growth.

Rotation is highly localized, led by Financials, which gained +1 spot to reach rank 8 with a momentum score of 0.61. Conversely, defensive and growth-adjacent sectors are fading. Communication Services dropped -1 spot to rank 9 (momentum 0.27), and Energy slipped -1 spot to rank 2 (momentum 0.44), reflecting a slight cooling in commodity-linked momentum. Meanwhile, Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom of the market (rank 11, momentum 0.26).

## Strength
* **Concentrated Breadth:** Only 3 out of 11 sectors (Technology, Industrials, and Financials) are currently "all-green," showing positive performance across all short- and long-term timeframes.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Technology (momentum 0.99) and Industrials (momentum 0.79) remain the top sustained sectors across 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month rankings.
* **Financials Join the Leaders:** Financials have achieved all-green status, supported by a momentum score of 0.61, indicating broad-based positive performance across all measured periods.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Technology and Financials were the only sectors to improve their rankings over the last 5 sessions, each climbing +1 spot to ranks 1 and 8, respectively.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Technology leads all groups with a momentum score of 0.986 (YTD rank 1), followed by Industrials at 0.786 (YTD rank 3) and Financials at 0.614 (YTD rank 8).
* **Momentum Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical is the weakest sector in the market with a momentum score of 0.257 (YTD rank 11), closely followed by Communication Services at 0.271 (YTD rank 9).

## Divergences
* **Financials Disconnect:** Financials are showing short-term strength as an all-green group and top gainer (+1 spot), yet they still lag significantly in overall YTD performance at rank 8.
* **Energy Slippage:** Energy is one of the top losers over the last 5 sessions (-1 spot), but it retains a highly resilient overall position at rank 2 with a momentum score of 0.44.
* **No Fragile All-Greens:** There are no active early-warning divergences or fragile ratings among the all-green leaders (Technology, Industrials, Financials), suggesting their current uptrends remain stable.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Tech hardware and industrial infrastructure continue to dominate with flawless "all-green" momentum, while heavy energy and defensive grocery staples experience sharp weekly rotations lower.

The market's core leadership remains highly concentrated in technology hardware and industrial manufacturing. Currently, 32 of 144 industry groups maintain "all-green" status across all time horizons (weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD). This charge is led by Computer Hardware (momentum 0.999) and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (momentum 0.985), with strong support from capital-goods sectors like Electrical Equipment & Parts and Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery. 

Meanwhile, active weekly rotation is lifting beaten-down areas. Biotechnology and Specialty Industrial Machinery both surged 21 spots in the rankings, while Uranium gained 20 spots. This capital is primarily rotating out of fossil fuels and defensive consumer areas, as Coking Coal plummeted 31 spots, Grocery Stores fell 28 spots, and Thermal Coal dropped 23 spots.

## Strength
* **Robust Breadth:** 32 of 144 industry groups are "all-green," signaling positive performance across all short- and long-term timeframes.
* **Tech Dominance:** Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.99 momentum), Electronic Components (0.96), and Semiconductors (0.95) anchor the market's strongest cohort.
* **Industrial Backbone:** Electrical Equipment & Parts (0.98 momentum), Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery (0.94), and Metal Fabrication (0.91) show sustained strength across 1, 3, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Weekly Gainers:** Biotechnology (+21 spots, rank 70, momentum 0.71), Specialty Industrial Machinery (+21 spots, rank 24, momentum 0.84), and Uranium (+20 spots, rank 55, momentum 0.57) led the weekly acceleration.
* **Sharpest Declines:** Coking Coal fell 31 spots to rank 101 (momentum 0.36), followed closely by Grocery Stores (-28 spots, rank 112) and Thermal Coal (-23 spots, rank 111).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Computer Hardware (0.999) and Semiconductor Equipment (0.985) remain the top YTD momentum leaders, while Consulting Services (0.061) and IT Services (0.087) continue to lag at the bottom of the rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups showing early signs of weakness include Steel (momentum 0.66, rank -9 in 5d), Apparel Manufacturing (momentum 0.61, rank -8 in 5d), and Trucking (momentum 0.73, rank -5 in 5d).
* **Emerging Laggards:** Low-momentum industries showing sudden rank improvements include Airports & Air Services (rank +14, momentum 0.40), Utilities - Independent Power Producers (rank +14, momentum 0.46), and Credit Services (rank +11, momentum 0.43).
